text: Further trouble occurred at Hull to-dry. The police charged the strikers with their batons in the City Square. Several were injured, seven being treated in the infirm.

The War Office states that no troops have yet been called up to aid the civil power except as guards at vulnerable points.

label: text
text: Britain, the Archbishop of Canterbury issued an appeal to all parties in the present crisis to resume negotiations, urging simultaneously and concurrently, firstly, that the Trade Union Congress cancel the general strike; secondly, that the Government renew its offer of assistance to the coal industry for a short period; and, thirdly, that the coal owners withdraw their new wares scale recently issued.

label: text
text: The British Worker appears half of yesterday's size. It declares that the Cabinet has stopped the supply of news print.

label: text
text: Three important London hospitals lack electricity owing to the Stepney power-station cutting off the supply: The British "Gazette" in this connection says that it shows the "incompetence of the Trade Union Congress, who promised that there would be no interference with the hospitals."

label: text
text: Numerous strikens have been sentenced to six months' imprisonment with hard labour for interfering with the Police.

label: text
text: A Moscow report says that the Soviet General Council of Trade Unions has transferred two million roubles to the Trade Union Congress as a second instalment of the collection among the Soviet Unions.

label: text
text: No. Poulton. Publicity Chairman of the Trade Unions Congress states that the Council had heard nothing about the Red International financial assistance. It was impossible to say what would be the attitude of the Council if a gift were offered.

label: text
text: Failing to suppress the strikers' attempt to interfere with a volunteer bus in Cardiff the police charged with their truncheons. Some women were trampled in the stampede. Two persons were injured and one arrested.

label: text
text: The "British Gazette" contends that the fact that the "British Worker" is published entirely by Trade Unionists proves that the strike is purely political and aimed at the newspapers whose opinions the Trade Union Congress disapproves.

label: text
text: It states that apart from the miners the strikers do not exceed a million of whom vast numbers were ordered to strike without being consulted.

label: text
text: The issue has ceased to be industrial and has become political and constitutional.

label: text
text: The chief apostle of the labour general headquarters, Mr. Ernest Bevin, of the Transport and General Workers' Union, is the real commander-in-Chief of the general strike.

label: text
text: It is explained that the Danish sympathy strike cannot be fixed for a week and will not begin for a fortnight at the earliest.

label: text
text: The Trade Union Congress in an official statement states that local strike organisations have been authorised to meet employers and offer a supply of light and power for houses, streets, shops, and social services.

label: text
text: The statement emphasises that the Council does not challenge the Constitution and is not desirous of undermining Parliamentary institutions.

label: text
text: The Trade Union lenders have cancelled their continental engagement. Mr. Cook is not going to Ostend.

text: The Executive Committee of the Danish Trade Unions' to-day gave the Employers' Association preliminary notice of a strike in support of the British strikers.

text: Coal freights to the Mediterranean have been reduced fifteen per cent. Freights have slumped in spite of the rush, and a vast tonnage is available.

text: The price of bunker coal in the New Waterway for ships in bullast has risen to $24/ and for loaded ships $26/

In a riot at Glasgow there was injured a police sergeant who went to hospital suffering from head injuries and concussion. He was struck with a stone: A youth who dashed through a shattered window was seriously hurt.

text: Further disturbances occurred in Edinburgh last night, the mob-stoning the Corporation bases. The Police charged the demonstrators and arrested nine.

label: text
text: There was rioting in Middlesbrough last night.

label: text
text: Official details show that heavy lorries were chained to rails in an attempt to wreck a late passenger train. A crowd prevented the closing of a level crossing, and the gates were invaded. A passenger station was wrecked and also a goods station. Serious damage was done.

label: text
text:
In response to the Mayor's appeal Naval ratings cleared the line for traffic after several hours work.
The great trek to the City and westward on the fourth morning of the strike was most disagreeable, but there is no great diminution of the number of pedestrians using the attenuated service. Trains from many districts relieved the situation. Five hundred trains ran on the Southern Railway yesterday, as indicating the improvement in long-distance railway communications.

label: text
text: Twenty-two arrests were made, and it is stunted the disorders were entirely due to rowdies and not by strikers, who resent the disturbances.

label: text
text: to-day's "Yorkshire Post" was on sale in London at an early hour. The continental "Daily Mail" was distributed to London and Suburb. The most noteworthy development is the withdrawal by workers of the Union facilities for distribution of food and supplies from well-known caterers such as Lyons, but an army of volunteers are carrying on the distribution. At Edinburgh the Police, with batons drawn, repeatedly cleared the thoroughfares, but order was not restored until Mounted Police were called out. Many windows were smashed, including those of many business premises.

British Newspapers.
The Press situation continues to improve following the London papers publishing emergency editions to-day by the “Times,” “Daily Telegraph,” “Daily Express,” “Daily Mirror and “Daily Mail.”

label: text
text: Tram-cars and buses are running and the railway services are increased. OFFICIALS INDICTED.

text: The Federal Grand Jury have indicted Henry Daugherty, ex-Attorney-General, and Thomas Miller, ex-Allen Property Customer, for a conspiracy in connection with the disposal of the property of the American Metals Company.

text: The indictment is that it was part of the conspiracy to enable Daugherty, Miller, and others to receive from the claimants securities of $391,000 which were paid in for putting through the transfer deal.

label: text
text: The Rhenish-Westphalian Steel Trust officially exists to-day and is known as the Vereinigte Stahlwerke Ekiengesellschaft. It formally took over the Phoenix, Rheinstahl, Gelsenkirchen, Bochumverein, Deutsch-Luxemburg, Van Der Zypenwissen and Thyssen concerns. The managing director is Dr. Voegler. The capital is eight hundred million marks.

label: text
text: Further provincial newspapers are reappouring, and the Newspaper Society, in a statement, says the Provincial Press has vigorously replied to the attempt to muzzle it. Nearly every provincial newspaper from which information is received is publishing, and, in very many cases, editions and sizes are normal.

text: In several important centres it is reported that printing stuffs have refused to act unconstitutionally and have either remained at work or have returned after a brief absence.

label: text
text: Following the refusal of the Newport (Monmouth): Corporation to discontinue the supply of electrical power to industrial concerns, the strike committee have advised the withdrawal of men from the Power Station and operatives have been notified they must cease work this afternoon.

label: text
text: A further indication of railway improvement was shown in the special train bringing 550 liner passengers from Plymouth to London this afternoon.

label: text
text: The employees of the Newcastle Electric Supply Company struck last night, but the emergency staff are carrying on. Supply of power is uninterrupted.

label: text
text: A significant statement was made by the Speaker in the House of Commons, arising out of an enquiry whether arrangements will be made to enable the House to continue in session.

label: text
text:
Notwithstanding the absence of a regular staff responsible for the ordinary services of the House, the Speaker said he regretted it was a fact that the men engaged on the staff of the principal services of the House had been withdrawn.
He assured the House he would not allow the House to be disabled.
If it became necessary he would conduct the House without any printing or electric light.

text: The League of Nations Health Committee has adopted the second part of the Medical Director's report on his voyage to the Far East relating to the work of the Singapore Epidemiological and Intelligence Bureau, and passed a number of resolutions concerning, interalia, the development of the League's epidemiological service and the establishment of close contact with the Japanese public health service activities.

label: text
text: The report pays a tribute to the notable services of the Bureau to Eastern health administration, especially in having kept them promptly informed in regard to a serious cholera outbreak in several Asiatic ports during the past twelve months.

In spite of the strike the British delegation, headed by Lord Cecil, is leaving, for Geneva to-morrow, travelling by air to Paris to attend the meeting of the Committee on the composition of the Council of the League on Monday and thereafter the preliminary Disarmament Committee and the ordinary Council meeting in June at which Sir Austen Chamberlain will preside.
